title: Nutrigenomic influence of a curcumin-supplemented high glycemic diet on hippocampal microvasculature in male C57BL/6J mice.
authors: Balbuena, Emilio; Rutkowsky, Jennifer M; Nuthikattu, Saivageethi; Villablanca, Amparo C; Milenkovic, Dragan
one_liner_zh: 该研究分析姜黄素对高糖饮食小鼠海马微血管的转录组影响，仅涉及转录因子与代谢物的对接分析，非核心蛋白质-DNA互作体系，方法以转录组和简单对接为主，与本课题关联较弱。
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Curcumin, a dietary polyphenol primarily derived from turmeric, has potent antioxidant and anti-inflammatory capabilities against diet-related chronic diseases. A high glycemic diet (HGD) has been shown to contribute to cognitive decline and dysfunction of murine brain microvasculature. The goal of our study was to elucidate the multi-genomic effects of curcumin on hippocampal microvessels in mice during consumption of a high glycemic diet. METHODS: Male C57BL/6J mice were fed a low glycemic diet (LGD, 12% sucrose/weight), a high glycemic diet (HGD, 34% sucrose), or a HGD with 0.2% curcumin (HGD + Curc) for 12 weeks. Global transcriptomic profiles, including protein coding and non-coding genes, of laser-captured endothelial microvessels of the hippocampus were analyzed via microarrays. Bioinformatic tools were utilized to uncover networks and functional pathways of differentially expressed genes modulated by curcumin as well as interactivity between transcription factors and major curcumin metabolites via in silico docking analysis. RESULTS: The HGD + Curc treatment influenced the differential expression of 1887 genes compared to HGD alone, which included messenger RNAs, microRNAs, long noncoding RNAs, and small nucleolar RNAs. Of these modulated genes, 307 overlapped and were negatively correlated with the fold change expression of the HGD versus LGD comparison. These protein coding and non-coding gene targets regulated by HGD+Curc were involved in pathways related to neurodegeneration, oxidative phosphorylation, blood-brain barrier permeability, cell signaling, and cellular metabolism. DISCUSSION/CONCLUSION: The results from this study show that curcumin induces complex nutrigenomic modifications that could elucidate its neuroprotective effect against hippocampal microvascular dysfunction induced by a high glycemic diet.
abstract_zh: 引言：姜黄素（curcumin）是一种主要来源于姜黄（turmeric）的膳食多酚，具有针对饮食相关慢性疾病的强效抗氧化和抗炎能力。高血糖饮食（high glycemic diet, HGD）已被证明会导致小鼠脑微血管的认知功能下降和功能障碍。本研究旨在阐明姜黄素在高血糖饮食摄入期间对小鼠海马微血管的多基因组效应。方法：雄性C57BL/6J小鼠分别饲喂低血糖饮食（LGD，12%蔗糖/重量）、高血糖饮食（HGD，34%蔗糖）或含0.2%姜黄素的HGD（HGD + Curc），持续12周。通过微阵列分析激光捕获的海马内皮微血管的全局转录组谱，包括蛋白质编码和非编码基因。利用生物信息学工具揭示姜黄素调节的差异表达基因的网络和功能通路，并通过计算机模拟对接分析转录因子与主要姜黄素代谢物之间的相互作用。结果：与单独HGD相比，HGD + Curc处理影响了1887个基因的差异表达，包括信使RNA、微RNA、长链非编码RNA和小核仁RNA。在这些调节基因中，307个与HGD与LGD比较的倍数变化表达重叠且呈负相关。这些由HGD+Curc调控的蛋白质编码和非编码基因靶点涉及神经退行性变、氧化磷酸化、血脑屏障通透性、细胞信号传导和细胞代谢相关通路。讨论/结论：本研究结果表明，姜黄素诱导复杂的营养基因组学修饰，这可能阐明其对高血糖饮食诱导的海马微血管功能障碍的神经保护作用。
